formation.title: The Birth of Livonia
formation.text:
The crusaders have raised their banner over the Baltic. From the stone walls of Riga to the forest castles of Dorpat, a new Christian realm takes shape on the eastern shore of the Mare Balticum. But two visions compete for the soul of this young nation. The knights of the Order see Livonia as a bastion of militant Christianity: a frontier where the sword serves the cross, where every conquered acre brings another pagan soul to Christ. The merchants of Riga and the Hanseatic cities see something different: a gateway to the riches of the East, where amber, timber, and furs flow westward and silver flows back. Which vision shall prevail?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: By sword and cross, we shall hold this land.

modifiers.name: Sword and Cross
modifiers.text: The Livonian state was born from the clash of steel and the fervor of faith. German crusaders carved a Christian realm from pagan wilderness, raising the cross above every castle and cathedral from Riga to Reval. The Order's mounted knights and fanatical devotion to the conversion of the Baltic peoples define our national purpose.

options.text: The counting house serves God as well as the chapel.

modifiers.name: Baltic Emporium
modifiers.text: Riga, Dorpat, and Reval are not merely fortresses: they are the great warehouses of the northern world. Amber, timber, furs, and grain flow down the Daugava and Dvina to our harbors, where Hanseatic merchants weigh them against cloth, salt, and silver from the west. The wealth of the Baltic flows through Livonian hands.

advances.name: Schwertbrüder
advances.text: The Livonian Brothers of the Sword, the Schwertbrüder, were the original crusading order of the Baltic, founded in 1202. Their defeat at Saule in 1236 led to their absorption into the Teutonic Order, but their fanatical spirit lives on in Livonian military tradition.

event.title: The Battle of Saule
event.text: In 1236, the Livonian Brothers of the Sword marched south against the Samogitians and Semigallians. At Saule, the pagan warriors ambushed the crusader column in difficult terrain. The defeat was catastrophic: the Master of the Order and fifty knights fell. The Pope dissolved the Brothers of the Sword, and the survivors merged with the Teutonic Order to form the Livonian branch. From this disaster, a harder and more disciplined military order emerged, one that would hold the Baltic frontier for three more centuries.

options.text: From defeat, we forge a stronger blade.

advances.name: Ordensburg Tradition
advances.text: The Livonian Order built over 150 stone castles across the Baltic: massive Ordensburgen that served as military bases, administrative centers, and symbols of German dominion over the conquered lands.

advances.name: Baltic Amber
advances.text: The shores of the eastern Baltic yield Europe's finest amber: fossilized tree resin prized since antiquity for jewelry, medicine, and trade. Livonian merchants control the processing and export of this golden treasure.

advances.name: Terra Mariana
advances.text: The Land of the Virgin Mary: the name given by Pope Innocent III to the crusader territories in Livonia. The religious mission to convert the Baltic pagans is the moral foundation of the Livonian state.

advances.name: Livonian Wax Trade
advances.text: Beeswax from the vast forests of Livonia is indispensable for the churches and courts of western Europe. Livonian merchants ship thousands of tons annually: the candles of Christendom burn with Baltic fire. The wax is cut from hives hollowed in the living trees of the forest.

advances.name: Hanseatic Kontore
advances.text: Riga joined the Hanseatic League in 1282, establishing trading posts, Kontore, that linked the Baltic to the great commercial networks of northern Europe. These warehouses and merchant houses are the engines of Livonian prosperity.

advances.name: Cathedral Schools
advances.text: The bishops of Livonia founded cathedral schools in Riga, Dorpat, and Reval: the first institutions of higher learning in the Baltic. German scholarship, Latin letters, and theological training flowed from these schools into the wider society.

advances.name: Landtag of Walk
advances.text: The Livonian Diet, signed into being at Walk in 1435, created a governing assembly for the fractious confederation. Representatives of the Order, the bishops, the cities, and the vassals meet to resolve disputes and coordinate defense.

event.title: The Landtag of Walk
event.text: On the 4th of December 1435, the assembled estates of Livonia gathered in the town of Walk to sign the Livonian Confederation agreement. The Archbishop of Riga, the bishops of Courland, Dorpat, and Ösel-Wiek, the representatives of the Livonian Order, and the vassals of the land have all set their seals to this document. The Livonian Diet, the Landtag, provides a forum where the competing interests of the Order, the Church, and the cities can be reconciled without bloodshed. It is an imperfect compromise, but it binds this fractious confederation into something resembling a state.

options.text: May the Landtag preserve our unity.

advances.name: Baltic Timber Trade
advances.text: The vast pine and oak forests of Livonia produce timber, tar, and pitch for the shipyards of Europe. Rafts of logs float down the Daugava to Riga, where they are processed and shipped to England, Holland, and beyond.

advances.name: Livonian Flax
advances.text:
Livonian flax is spun into linen of exceptional quality, exported through Riga and Reval to markets across northern Europe. The flax fields of Latvia and Estonia sustain a thriving textile industry.

Available in: Packhaus

advances.name: Riga Stadtrecht
advances.text: The Hamburg city law adopted by Riga governs commerce, property, and civic life. Under this legal framework, Riga's burghers enjoy privileges that attract merchants and artisans from across the German-speaking world.

advances.name: The Livonian Reformation
advances.text: Livonia was the first territory outside the Holy Roman Empire to adopt the Reformation. From 1521, Luther's ideas spread rapidly through Riga, Reval, and Dorpat, transforming the religious landscape of the Baltic.

event.title: The Reformation Reaches Livonia
event.text: In 1521, Andreas Knopken returned from Germany bearing Luther's teachings to the churches of Riga. Within three years, the Reformation swept through every major city in Livonia: Riga, Reval, Dorpat. Melchior Hoffmann preaches fiery sermons in Wolmar, and crowds gather to hear the new gospel. The Riga City Council has banned services in the cathedral, confiscated church property, and closed the monasteries. Some reformers call for measured adoption of the new faith; others demand the destruction of every icon and altar that recalls the old order. In November 1524, iconoclastic mobs stormed the churches. Shall we channel this fury or contain it?

options.text: Let reform proceed through reason and law.

modifiers.name: Livonian Reformation
modifiers.text: Livonia was among the first lands outside the Empire to embrace the teachings of Luther. The old religious order dissolves as new ideas take root in Riga's printing houses and lecture halls.

options.text: Tear down the idols; purify the faith by fire.

modifiers.name: Riga Iconoclasm
modifiers.text: The reformers have swept through the churches of Riga with hammer and torch, smashing icons, closing monasteries, and confiscating ecclesiastical property. The old order is destroyed root and branch: a violent purification that leaves no room for the past.

advances.name: Livonian Landknechte
advances.text: German pike-and-shot infantry adapted to Baltic warfare: trained to fight in the forests and marshes of the eastern frontier, where heavy cavalry cannot operate.

advances.name: Baltic Grain Trade
advances.text: Livonian grain (rye, wheat, and barley) feeds the growing cities of western Europe. Riga's granaries are the breadbasket of the Baltic, funneling harvests from the hinterland to hungry markets abroad.

advances.name: Between Three Crowns
advances.text: Livonia sits at the crossroads of Russian, Polish-Lithuanian, and Swedish ambitions. Survival demands diplomatic agility, playing each power against the others, buying time with treaties, and maintaining a precarious independence.

advances.name: Stone Castle Network
advances.text: Over 150 stone castles and fortified manors dot the Livonian landscape: from the massive Ordensburgen of the knights to the episcopal palaces of the bishops. This fortress network is the backbone of Baltic defense.

advances.name: Livonian Fur Trade
advances.text:
The forests of Livonia yield beaver, marten, fox, and squirrel pelts prized in the courts and markets of Europe. Livonian merchants dominate the fur trade from the interior to the harbors of Riga and Reval.

Available in: Packhaus

advances.name: Hakenschützen
advances.text: The hook gun, the Hakenbüchse, is a staple of Livonian fortress defense. Resting the heavy barrel on a wall hook, these gunners deliver accurate fire from castle ramparts and field fortifications.

advances.name: Livonian Reiters
advances.text: The mounted pistoleer tradition descends from the Order's heavy cavalry. Armed with wheel-lock pistols and trained in the caracole, these Reiters combine Livonian horsemanship with modern firepower.

advances.name: Secularization
advances.text: The transformation from crusading military order to secular duchy: the end of monastic rule and the beginning of princely government. Under Gotthard Kettler, the last Master became the first Duke.

advances.name: Riga Grain Staple
advances.text: Riga's staple right requires that all grain passing through the city be offered for sale in its market before export. This monopoly enriches the city's burghers and fills the ducal coffers.

advances.name: Livonian Privilegium
advances.text: The rights and privileges of the Baltic German nobility, the Ritterschaften, are the foundation of Livonian governance. In exchange for military service and administrative loyalty, the nobles enjoy wide autonomy over their estates.

advances.name: Modern Fortifications
advances.text: The arrival of gunpowder warfare demands new defensive architecture. Bastioned walls, angled ravelins, and earthwork ramparts replace the medieval towers, transforming Livonian cities into modern fortresses.

advances.name: Courland Fleet
advances.text: Duke Jacob Kettler built a navy of over forty warships from the shipyards of Windau and Libau. This remarkable fleet (mounting over 1,400 cannons) carried the Courlandish flag to colonies on the Gambia River and Tobago.

event.title: Courland's Colonial Ambition
event.text: Duke Jacob Kettler has transformed the sleepy Duchy of Courland into a maritime power. From the shipyards of Windau, a fleet of over forty warships has been launched, mounting more than fourteen hundred cannons. In 1651, Courlandish forces built Fort Jacob on the Gambia River. In 1654, the double-decker warship Wappen der Herzogin sailed to Tobago with 124 soldiers and eighty colonist families, establishing New Courland. This tiny duchy, barely fifty thousand souls, now flies its flag on two continents. But the dream is fragile. Sweden threatens war, and the colonial ventures drain the treasury. Shall we press forward or consolidate what we have?

options.text: The seas shall carry the Courlandish flag to every shore.

modifiers.name: Courland's Ambition
modifiers.text: From the shipyards of Windau and Libau, a fleet rises that will carry the Courlandish flag to distant shores. Fort Jacob on the Gambia and New Courland on Tobago await: the smallest state in Europe dares to build a colonial empire.

options.text: Our wealth lies in the Baltic, not in tropical fevers.

modifiers.name: Courland's Prudence
modifiers.text: The Duchy's fleet is better employed protecting our Baltic trade routes and enriching our harbors than chasing distant colonial dreams. Let others waste their treasure on tropical fever. We shall grow wealthy at home.

advances.name: Kettler's Manufactures
advances.text: Under Duke Jacob Kettler, Courland became an industrial center. Ironworks, sawmills, tar distilleries, and rope walks sprang up across the duchy: a proto-industrial revolution on the Baltic shore.

advances.name: Colonial Ventures
advances.text: The tiny Duchy of Courland, barely fifty thousand souls, dared to build a colonial empire. Fort Jacob on the Gambia and New Courland on Tobago were improbable outposts of Baltic ambition in the tropics.

advances.name: Amber Road
advances.text:
The ancient amber trade route, stretching from the Baltic coast to the Mediterranean, has been a source of wealth for millennia. Under Courland's stewardship, the processing and export of Baltic amber reaches its zenith. Amber is turned on the lathe and set in silver for the courts of Europe.

Available in: Bernsteinkammer

advances.name: Ritterschaften
advances.text: The Baltic German noble corporations (the Ritterschaften of Livonia, Estonia, Courland, and Ösel) govern the provinces through their Landtage. This corporate nobility shapes law, taxation, and administration across the Baltic.

advances.name: Courland Naval Gunnery
advances.text:
Courland's fleet punched far above its weight thanks to the quality of its naval gunnery. Duke Jacob personally oversaw cannon founding at Courland's ironworks, producing some of the finest naval guns in the Baltic.

Available in: Eisenhammer

advances.name: Baltic Enlightenment
advances.text: Johann Gottfried Herder (philosopher, theologian, and pioneer of romantic nationalism) spent five formative years teaching at Riga's cathedral school. His ideas on folk culture and national identity would transform European thought.

advances.name: Agrarian Reform
advances.text: The gradual emancipation of the Baltic peasantry and the modernization of agriculture: from feudal corvée labor to free tenancy. New crop rotations, drainage projects, and scientific farming increase yields and population.

advances.name: Port of Riga
advances.text: Riga's harbor, commanding the mouth of the Daugava, expands to accommodate the growing volume of Baltic commerce. New wharves, warehouses, and customs houses transform the medieval port into a modern commercial hub.

advances.name: Baltic German Identity
advances.text: The Baltic Germans (descendants of the crusaders, merchants, and clerics who built Livonia) develop a distinct cultural identity. Neither purely German nor purely Baltic, they are a unique civilization forged by seven centuries on the frontier.

advances.name: Livonian Jäger
advances.text: Professional light infantry for the modern age: fast-moving riflemen who combine the frontier traditions of the Baltic with the discipline of European line tactics.

advances.name: Industrial Timber
advances.text: Steam-powered sawmills transform the Baltic timber industry. Where once logs were laboriously shaped by hand, mechanical saws now produce standardized lumber for export, feeding the construction boom of industrial Europe.

destiny.name: Livonian Destiny
destiny.text: The state of Livonia stands at the crossroads of the Baltic world. Whether by sword or by silver, our destiny awaits. But first, we must prove that this young nation can endure.

event.title: The Destiny of Livonia
event.text: Livonia has been forged from the scattered territories of the Baltic: a realm where German knights, Hanseatic merchants, and Baltic peoples coexist under a single banner. But the mere act of formation is not enough. The question that now confronts us is fundamental: what kind of state shall Livonia become? The path forward will define not just our borders, but our very identity as a nation.

destiny.name: The Northern Crusade
destiny.text: The crusader spirit demands expansion. Conquer the pagan stronghold of Samogitia and the Teutonic capital of Konigsberg to forge a unified crusader state across the eastern Baltic.

event.title: The Northern Crusade Renewed
event.text: The knights have ridden south into Samogitia and east into Prussia. Where once the pagans held sway, the cross now rises above every fortress and village. Konigsberg, the ancient seat of the Teutonic Order, flies our banner. The crusader state is reborn: not as a scattered confederation of bishops and knights, but as a unified realm with the strength to expand further still.

destiny.name: Drang nach Osten
destiny.text: The drive to the east continues. Pskov and Polotsk, the gateway cities to the vast Russian hinterland, are taken, and five Ordensburgen stand to hold the march.

conditions.text: An Ordensburg stands in at least 5 of our locations

event.title: The Drive to the East
event.text: Pskov has fallen. Polotsk is ours. The ancient trading cities of the Russian frontier now answer to Livonian authority. Our armies stand deep in territory that was once the domain of Orthodox princes and Slavic boyars. But how shall we govern these new conquests? Some urge the zeal of the crusade: forced conversion, German settlement, the complete transformation of the conquered lands. Others counsel patience: the establishment of order through military discipline and administrative efficiency, allowing the new subjects to be gradually absorbed.

options.text: Fill the east with German settlers and churches.

modifiers.name: Crusader Zeal
modifiers.text: The fervor of the northern crusade fuels Livonian expansion. German settlers and missionaries pour into the conquered territories, but the costs of ceaseless warfare strain the treasury.

options.text: Establish military order on the frontier.

modifiers.name: Frontier Order
modifiers.text: The conquered eastern territories are governed through strict military order: fortified garrisons, disciplined patrols, and systematic administration. The frontier is secure, though building in the new territories is expensive.

destiny.name: Dominium Maris Baltici
destiny.text: Novgorod, the ancient seat of Russian trade, falls, and with it Vilnius, capital of Lithuania, and Kaunas, the castle on the Niemen. With these conquests Livonia becomes the undisputed master of the eastern Baltic: a crusader empire stretching from the Gulf of Finland to the Niemen.

event.title: Dominium Maris Baltici
event.text: Novgorod, the legendary city of a thousand churches, has submitted to Livonian power. Vilnius, seat of the Lithuanian grand dukes, flies our banner. From the Gulf of Finland to the forests of Samogitia, from the shores of Courland to the gates of Muscovy, the crusader state commands an empire. The eastern Baltic is a Livonian lake. But with empire comes the question of its character. Shall we rule as the iron cross demanded: with the uncompromising authority of the Order? Or shall we establish a Livonian peace, governing our diverse subjects through strength tempered by pragmatism?

options.text: Under the iron cross, all submit.

modifiers.name: Under the Iron Cross
modifiers.text: The iron discipline of the crusading order governs the Livonian empire. Subject peoples submit to an unyielding authority that tolerates no dissent. But the burden of perpetual vigilance weighs on a war-weary nation.

options.text: A Livonian peace shall govern the east.

modifiers.name: Pax Livonica
modifiers.text: The Livonian peace governs the eastern Baltic through pragmatic strength. Conquered territories are brought to order through efficient administration and the promise of stability, rewarding those who submit and enriching the realm through plunder.

destiny.name: Hanseatic Gateway
destiny.text: Bring Danzig, the greatest port on the southern Baltic, under Livonian control and amass the capital to fund a commercial empire. Riga and Danzig together command the flow of grain, timber, and amber across the northern seas.

event.title: The Hanseatic Gateway
event.text: Danzig is ours. The greatest port on the southern Baltic, where the Vistula pours Poland's grain into the holds of a thousand merchant ships, now operates under Livonian authority. With Riga commanding the Daugava and Danzig commanding the Vistula, we control the two mightiest river-trade arteries of the northern world. The counting houses are full, the warehouses stacked to the rafters. The Baltic Emporium is taking shape.

options.text: The wealth of two rivers flows through our hands.

destiny.name: Baltic Warehouse
destiny.text: Establish Livonia as the central warehouse of the Baltic. Take Reval, where the goods of the Novgorod trade are warehoused, and build it up, ensure amber flows through our capital market, and accumulate the wealth that transforms a trading post into an emporium.

conditions.text: We own Reval (Tallinn) and its development is at least 31

children.text: Amber is produced in the market
Amber is traded in the market

event.title: The Livonian Warehouse
event.text: Livonia has become the central warehouse of the Baltic world. Our bankers extend credit from Riga to London, our amber is prized in every court, and our merchants dominate the trade in grain, timber, and furs. But two commercial philosophies compete for dominance. The amber merchants advocate monopoly, controlling the supply of Baltic amber from mine to market, setting prices that the world must pay. The port masters advocate openness, making our harbors the freest in Europe, where any merchant can trade without restriction, trusting that volume will generate more wealth than any monopoly.

options.text: Control the amber, control the market.

modifiers.name: Amber Monopoly
modifiers.text: Livonia controls the amber trade from mine to market, setting prices, regulating exports, and reaping enormous profits from Europe's appetite for Baltic gold. The assimilation of subject peoples proceeds rapidly under merchant-driven cultural integration.

options.text: Open our ports to the commerce of the world.

modifiers.name: Free Port Charter
modifiers.text: Livonian harbors are the freest in Europe: any merchant, any flag, any cargo. The policy attracts traders from across the continent, but a nation built on open trade finds it harder to justify war.

destiny.name: Supreme Emporium
destiny.text: Conquer Lubeck itself, the queen of the Hanse, and make Livonia the supreme commercial power of northern Europe. Build Riga up into the great port of the north and fill the treasury to overflowing.

conditions.text: We own Riga and its development is at least 53

event.title: The Supreme Emporium
event.text: Lubeck itself, the queen of the Hanseatic League, the city whose merchants once dictated the terms of trade across all of northern Europe, now answers to Livonia. The student has surpassed the master. From our harbors, ships carry Baltic goods to every corner of Europe and beyond. Our bankers finance wars and trade ventures from the North Sea to the Mediterranean. Riga has become what Venice is to the south: the indispensable nexus of commerce, the city without which nothing moves. Shall we rule this empire as merchant princes, a commercial aristocracy governing through wealth and influence? Or shall we make Riga the Venice of the North, a republic of traders where commerce itself is the highest law?

modifiers.name: Merchant Princes
modifiers.text: A commercial aristocracy governs Livonia: wealthy merchant families whose influence spans the courts and counting houses of northern Europe. Their diplomatic reach extends the Livonian trade network across the continent.

options.text: Riga shall be the Venice of the North.

modifiers.name: Baltic Venice
modifiers.text: Riga has become the Venice of the North: a republic of commerce where the flow of trade is the highest law. The city's wealth sustains a professional mercenary force, and the complacency of easy prosperity is kept at bay by the constant drive for new markets.

units.name: Schwertbrüder
units.text: The Sword Brothers: fanatical crusading infantry of the Livonian Order. These German warriors fight with the zealous fury of men who believe every battle is fought for the salvation of their souls.

units.name: Hakenschützen
units.text: Hook gunners: infantry armed with heavy arquebus-type weapons fired from wall hooks or portable rests. Devastating in siege defense and fortified positions, they embody Livonia's tradition of fortress warfare.

units.name: Courland Frigate
units.text: A fast, well-armed warship from the shipyards of Windau. Built under Duke Jacob Kettler's personal supervision, these frigates combine speed with firepower: designed for commerce raiding and colonial expeditions.

units.name: Livonian Reiter
units.text: Mounted pistoleers descended from the Order's cavalry tradition. Armed with wheel-lock pistols and trained in the caracole tactic, these riders harass enemy formations before closing for the charge.

units.name: Livonian Jäger
units.text: Professional light infantry trained in the forests of the Baltic: fast-moving riflemen who use terrain, ambush tactics, and marksmanship to outfight opponents. The culmination of Livonia's long frontier military tradition.

buildings.name: Ordensburg
buildings.text: A crusader castle of the Livonian Order: a massive stone fortification combining military garrison, administrative center, and chapel. These castles dominated the Baltic landscape for three centuries.

buildings.name: Hanseatic Kontor
buildings.text: A trading post of the Hanseatic League: warehouse, counting house, and merchant residence in one. Through these Kontore, the wealth of the Baltic hinterland flows to the markets of northern Europe.

buildings.name: Packhaus
buildings.text: A merchant's packing house on the quay, where the goods of the river trade are made fit for the sea. Each lot is sorted by sworn graders before it is shipped.

buildings.name: Forest Apiary
buildings.text: Hives are hollowed in living pines and oaks, each tree under its keeper's mark. The honey is eaten at home and the wax goes to the port. The more trees the keepers cut and tend, the more wax the forest yields.

where.text: The location's raw material is Beeswax

buildings.name: Domschule
buildings.text: A cathedral school where German clerics teach Latin, theology, and the liberal arts. These schools are the intellectual foundations of Livonian civilization, producing the administrators and clergy who govern the Baltic.

buildings.name: Windau Shipyard
buildings.text: The ducal shipyard at Windau (Ventspils), where Duke Jacob Kettler's fleet was constructed. At its peak, this yard launched warships that carried the Courlandish flag to Africa and the Caribbean.

buildings.name: Bernsteinkammer
buildings.text: An amber processing workshop where raw Baltic amber is sorted, polished, and carved into jewelry, devotional objects, and luxury goods for export to the courts and markets of Europe.

buildings.name: Vasallenburg
buildings.text: A fortified manor house of the Baltic German vassals: part residence, part garrison, part administrative center for the surrounding countryside. The backbone of rural defense and noble authority across Livonia.

buildings.name: Getreidelager
buildings.text: A grain warehouse on the Riga waterfront: storing, weighing, and grading the vast quantities of rye, wheat, and barley that flow from the Livonian hinterland to feed the cities of western Europe.

buildings.name: Dampfsägewerk
buildings.text: A steam-powered sawmill at a Baltic timber port. Iron blades driven by steam engines cut through the pine and oak logs floated down the rivers, and the forests of the land around it are felled faster to feed it.

where.text: The location's raw material is Lumber

buildings.name: Eisenhammer
buildings.text: A ducal hammer mill on a Courland stream. A water wheel drives the trip hammer and the bellows, bog iron and bar iron shipped from Sweden go into the forge, and muskets, anchors, nails and ship guns come out for the duke's fleet and for sale abroad.

buildings.name: Deutschordensschloss
buildings.text: A grand castle of the crusading order: part fortress, part palace, part seat of government. Its massive walls and towered keep dominate the landscape, projecting the power and permanence of the Livonian crusader state across the conquered territories.

buildings.name: Borsenhaus
buildings.text: A grand exchange house where the merchants of the Baltic conduct their business, negotiating prices, settling accounts, and arranging the shipment of goods from Riga to the markets of Europe. The commercial heart of the Livonian trade empire.

list.name: Landtag at Walk
list.text: The Livonian Confederation's diet, convened in 1419 at the initiative of Archbishop Johannes Ambundii at Walk (Volmar/Wolmar) and reconvened on a regular schedule until 1559. The four Estates (the Livonian Order, the prince-bishops of Riga, Dorpat, Ösel-Wiek, and Courland, the vassal Knighthoods, and the Hanseatic cities of Riga, Reval, and Dorpat) met to ratify common policy on coinage, war, treaties, and internal disputes. The Landtag was the only body that could speak for medieval Livonia as a whole; in practice it gave the secular and ecclesiastical lords a permanent veto over any single ruler's ambitions.

list.name: Ordens Konvent
list.text: The administrative structure of the Livonian branch of the Teutonic Order. The Landmeister (seated at Wenden, later Riga) presided over the Großgebietiger (the five great-officer collegium of Landmarschall, Großkomtur, Drapier, Spittler, and Tressler) while individual Komture commanded the Order's Kommenden, the Ordensburg fortresses that anchored the conquest from Riga to Narva. The Konvent system fused monastic chapter, military command, and territorial administration into a single celibate-brethren institution that ran the realm from the 1240s until secularization in 1561.

list.name: Hanseatic Stadtrat
list.text: The civic governance of Riga (chartered under Lübeck Law in 1201), Reval/Tallinn (1248), and Dorpat. The Rat (a self-perpetuating council of the wealthiest Low German merchant lineages) elected up to four Bürgermeister from its own number, sent representatives to the Hansetag at Lübeck, and administered Lübeck Law within the city walls. The Brotherhood of Blackheads, an association of unmarried foreign merchants whose statutes were ratified in Reval in 1407 and Riga in 1416, supplied urban militia, defended the towns during the Saint George's Night Uprising tradition, and served as the antechamber to full Rat membership. Their houses still stand in Tallinn and once stood in Riga.

list.name: Ritterschaft Vasallenrecht
list.text: The corporate self-administration of the Baltic German vassal nobility, organized into four Knighthoods: Harju-Viru in northern Estonia (de facto autonomous from 1252), Ösel-Wiek, Estland, and Livland. Each Knighthood maintained its own Mannbuch (vassal roll), Mannrichter court, and Wackenbuch survey of peasant dues, and assembled its members into a corporate body that mustered cavalry, ratified Knighthood law, and represented the vassal estate at the Walk Landtag. The Privilegium Sigismundi Augusti of 28 November 1561 codified these privileges into the Indigenat: the Baltic German right of self-administration that survived every change of sovereignty (Polish, Swedish, Russian) until the dissolutions of 1917 in Estland and 1920 in Livland.
